cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! Pixi and I are so glad you're here.

cues.caption: Last time: AI finds patterns, then guesses
cues.text: Last time, we learned that AI is maths, not magic. It finds patterns in lots of examples, and then it makes a guess. And sometimes, that guess is wrong!

cues.caption: Chapter 2 · Smart vs. Simple
cues.text: Today is chapter two of, What Is AI? It's called, Smart versus Simple.

cues.caption: Is every gadget with a button AI?
cues.text: Here's a puzzle for you. Is every gadget with a button, AI? Hmm. Let's find out.

cues.caption: 6:30 on a Saturday. Ring, ring!
cues.text: It's Saturday morning at Kabir's house. Ring, ring, ring! His alarm clock goes off at six thirty. Ugh. It's a holiday!

cues.caption: Mini: "This torch is so smart. It's AI!"
cues.text: Later, the power goes out. His little sister Mini grabs a torch, clicks it on, and shouts, wow! This torch is so smart. It must be AI!

cues.caption: Is a torch AI? What do you think?
cues.text: Is Mini right? Is a torch AI? What do you think?

cues.caption: Two kinds: simple and smart
cues.text: Let's find out. Because there are two kinds of programs. Simple ones, and smart ones. By the end of today, you'll tell them apart like a detective!

cues.caption: Simple programs follow FIXED RULES
cues.text: Simple programs follow fixed rules. A fixed rule is an instruction that never changes.

cues.caption: If the button is pressed → play a sound
cues.text: Like a doorbell. If the button is pressed, play a sound. Press it today. Ding dong! Press it next week. Ding dong! Exactly the same.

cues.caption: At 6:30 → ring. Every single day!
cues.text: Kabir's alarm clock has a fixed rule too. At six thirty, ring. Monday, ring. Saturday, ring. Even on his birthday, ring!

cues.caption: Torch: switch on → light on
cues.text: And Mini's torch? Switch on, light on. Switch off, light off. That's it. One fixed rule.

cues.caption: Simple programs never learn anything new
cues.text: Here's the key thing. A simple program never learns anything new. The alarm clock will never figure out that Kabir likes to sleep in on Saturdays.

cues.caption: Sunday, 6:30. What will the alarm do?
cues.text: Quick question. Tomorrow is Sunday, and Kabir really wants to sleep late. What will his alarm clock do at six thirty? Think!

cues.caption: Ring! The fixed rule never changes.
cues.text: Ring, ring, ring! Of course. It follows its fixed rule, no matter what. It can't learn that Sunday is different. Poor Kabir!

cues.caption: AI learns from examples, and changes
cues.text: Now, smart programs, like AI, are different. They learn from examples. And they change what they do, after seeing more examples.

cues.caption: Learning = getting better from more examples
cues.text: Learning here doesn't mean thinking like you do. It just means the program gets better at its job, by looking at more and more examples.

cues.caption: A voice assistant hears millions of voices
cues.text: Think of a voice assistant. At first, it might mix up your words. But it hears millions of voices. Voices from Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, and everywhere!

cues.caption: More examples → better at understanding
cues.text: Over time, it gets better at understanding all kinds of accents. More examples, better guesses!

cues.caption: Oops! You type "becuase"
cues.text: Here's another one. Spellcheck. You're typing a message to your nani. You want to type, because, but oops, the letters get mixed up.

cues.caption: Spellcheck learned words from lots of writing
cues.text: And spellcheck suggests, because! How does it know? It learned common words from lots and lots of writing.

cues.caption: Photo search learned from example photos
cues.text: Or photo search. Type dog in a photo app, and it finds all your dog pictures. It learned what dogs look like, from lots of example photos.

cues.caption: Video suggestions change as you watch more
cues.text: And remember Kabir's cricket cartoons? Video suggestions change too, as you watch more. Watch lots of animal videos, and soon, you'll see more animals!

cues.caption: Does it change after more examples?
cues.text: So here's a super question, to test any gadget. Does it change what it does, after more examples?

cues.caption: Yes → it may be AI
cues.text: If yes, it may be AI. Like the voice assistant, or spellcheck. They keep getting better with more examples.

cues.caption: No → a simple, fixed-rule program
cues.text: If no, it's a simple, fixed rule program. Like the doorbell. Does it have a screen? Is it expensive? Those questions don't help. Only this one does!

cues.caption: Sort it: fixed rule, or learns?
cues.text: Let's play, sort it! Fixed rule, or learns from examples?

cues.caption: Which ones learn from examples?
cues.text: Alarm clock. Spellcheck. Doorbell. Voice assistant. Calculator. Photo search. Which ones learn from examples? Pause, and think.

cues.caption: 3 follow fixed rules · 3 learn from examples
cues.text: The alarm clock, doorbell, and calculator follow fixed rules. Spellcheck, the voice assistant, and photo search learn from examples. How did you do? Oh, and a ceiling fan switch? Fixed rule too!

cues.caption: A DESIGNER writes and plans a program
cues.text: Now, one more big idea. Who makes all these programs? People! The person who writes and plans a program is called a designer.

cues.caption: People design simple programs AND AI
cues.text: People design the doorbell's simple rule. If pressed, play a sound. And people design AI too. They write the program, and they test it.

cues.caption: People choose the examples AI learns from
cues.text: People even choose the examples that AI learns from. Like picking thousands of cat photos, to teach it what a cat looks like.

cues.caption: AI doesn't build itself. People are in charge!
cues.text: So AI doesn't build itself out of nothing. Every AI has human designers. People are still in charge.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Is a torch AI? Why or why not?
cues.text: Remember Mini? Is a torch AI? Why, or why not? Pause the video, and think. Or write your answer on paper.

cues.caption: No! One fixed rule. It never learns or changes.
cues.text: No, it's not! A torch follows one fixed rule. Switch on, light on. It never learns from examples, and it never changes what it does. Sorry, Mini! Great thinking, champ.

cues.caption: Simple programs follow fixed rules
cues.text: Let's remember. Simple programs follow fixed rules, like a doorbell.

cues.caption: AI changes after seeing more examples
cues.text: AI changes what it does, after seeing more examples.

cues.caption: A torch is not AI. It just follows a switch.
cues.text: A torch is not AI. It just follows a switch.

cues.caption: People design both
cues.text: And people design both simple programs, and AI.

cues.caption: Chapter 2 done!
cues.text: Chapter two, done! Now you can tell smart from simple, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
